name: Mo Shuming
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time vice chairman) of Guangdong Mingcrown Group, Dongguan
profile: Dongguan-born entrepreneur who co-founded Guangdong Mingcrown Group (名冠集团) in 1994 with Mo Zhiming. The family conglomerate spans construction, real estate, steel/new materials (Huaguan), Xinhui Port logistics, hotels, schools and a golf club; it is now chaired by Mo Guanliang and ranks among Guangdong's top 500 companies.
interesting_fact: Mingcrown is pivoting into culture-tourism: in March 2026 it won Dongguan's first land auction of the year for RMB 730m to build the Mingcrown Oasis theme-park project, and signed a strategic deal with Tencent Cloud in April 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; the group site names him only as co-founder. A 2012 Xinhui district government page called him vice chairman of Mingcrown. Day-to-day leadership is now Mo Guanliang (chairman) and Mo Guanjing (president). Hurun listed him jointly with Yao Hesong. Best route is the group's corporate email.

name: Chen Wenli
current_role: Former director and co-founder of HNA Group (left the board in March 2020); no current public role found
profile: Chen Wenli was one of the founders of Hainan-based HNA Group in 1993, alongside Chen Feng, Wang Jian and Adam Tan. He held an individual HNA stake (Hurun rich list 2017-2019) and sat on the board. He left the board in March 2020 when a Hainan government working group took control. HNA later went through court-led restructuring in 2021, which wiped out the founders' equity.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HNA, which grew from a provincial airline into a global conglomerate that held stakes in Hilton, Deutsche Bank and Swissport during a record overseas buying spree that ended in 2017.
notes: Very low profile and likely not a viable guest. His wealth was tied to HNA equity that was largely erased in the 2021 bankruptcy restructuring, and other HNA founders were detained in 2021. Source for his 2020 board exit: https://www.mingtiandi.com/?p=43164. No personal channels found.

name: Rohini Nilekani
current_role: Chairperson, Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies; co-founder and director, EkStep Foundation
profile: Mumbai-born former journalist and author whose wealth comes from early Infosys shares held with her husband, Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani. She founded the water NGO Arghyam (2001), co-founded Akshara Foundation and Pratham Books, and now runs Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies, which funds civil society, water, climate, biodiversity and youth causes. She also hosts the Grassroots Nation podcast.
interesting_fact: She set up Arghyam in 2001 with a personal endowment of about Rs 150 crore. She chaired it for 20 years before stepping down in 2021, and she is regularly ranked among India's most generous women philanthropists.
deep_cut_fact: She started her career in 1980 as a reporter at the now-defunct Bombay Magazine, after a degree in French literature from Elphinstone College. In 1998 Penguin published her medical-thriller novel 'Stillborn'. She also writes children's stories (the Sringeri series) for Pratham Books, which she co-founded in 2004.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly: she writes columns, gives talks and hosts her own podcast, so a podcaster pitch could suit her. The best route is the RNP contact email. The X/LinkedIn/Instagram accounts listed are the foundation's, not her personal ones. Her angle is philanthropy and civil society rather than energy or data centres.

name: Huang Tengxin
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Zuoyou (Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture / 左右沙发)
profile: Hurun China lists Huang Tengxin (黄腾新) as the wealth holder behind Zuoyou, a furniture business. Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture (左右家私) is a sofa maker with about 4,000 staff and parks in Shenzhen, Huizhou, Anhui and Sichuan. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as its founder, who started making sofas in Shenzhen in 1986. No source found that links the name Huang Tengxin to the company.
interesting_fact: Zuoyou registered its brand in 1995 and opened China's first 'scenario-style' living-room furniture stores. In 2005 it signed former China women's volleyball head coach Chen Zhonghe as brand ambassador.
notes: Identity unresolved. Hurun's 'Huang Tengxin' may be a transliteration or listing error, or a relative or partner of founder Huang Huakun. Verify against Hurun's Chinese list before any outreach. Baidu and Sogou blocked automated lookups.

name: Dennis Erani
current_role: Private investor; 7.8% beneficial owner of Organogenesis Holdings (Nasdaq: ORGO)
profile: Dennis Erani is a passive ten-percent-group holder of Organogenesis, the Canton, MA regenerative-medicine and wound-care company in which the Ades and Erani families are the largest individual holders. The April 2026 proxy shows him with about 10.0m shares (7.8%), mostly held through family trusts. He holds no board or executive role.
interesting_fact: Organogenesis sells regenerative wound-care and surgical/sports-medicine products. Per the 2026 proxy, Alan Ades (17.3%), Albert Erani (13.9%) and Dennis Erani (7.8%) together hold about 39% of its shares.
notes: Essentially no public profile: no interviews, bio or social accounts found. He appears to be a member of the Erani family (Albert Erani is a separate 13.9% holder), but the exact relationship is unconfirmed. Company contacts reach Organogenesis, not him personally. His filed residential address is deliberately omitted.

name: Lin Xiuhao
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Heiniu Investment (黑牛投资)
profile: Hurun China (2017-2019) lists Lin Xiuhao (林秀浩) as the holder of 'Heiniu Investment' (黑牛 = Blackcow). The name points to Shantou's Black Cattle/Blackcow Food Co. (黑牛食品), a soy-milk and cereal maker whose listed shell was later renamed Visionox Technology, an OLED display maker. No source retrieved confirms Lin Xiuhao's own role.
interesting_fact: In July 2016 Black Cattle Food sold its whole food and beverage business (soy-milk powder, cereals, sesame paste, nut milks) for CNY 513m to Shenzhen Blackcow Capital Management, and the listed shell pivoted to tech. It is now Visionox, the OLED panel maker.
notes: Identity not verified. Chinese search engines (Baidu, Sogou) blocked automated access, and English sources only show Lin Xiuhai (possibly a relative) as a Blackcow/Visionox director. Confirm via Blackcow Food's pre-2018 annual reports on cninfo.com.cn before any outreach. Very private, with no personal channels.
